sections.section_name: Section C (Long Answer & Case Study Questions)

questions.question_text: Differentiate between mixtures and compounds across 5 distinct criteria.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Formation: Mixtures formed by physical mixing; Compounds by chemical bonding. 2. Composition: Mixtures have variable ratios; Compounds fixed ratios. 3. Properties: Mixtures retain constituent traits; Compounds display new traits. 4. Separation: Mixtures separated by physical methods; Compounds require chemical/electrical methods. 5. Energy: Mixtures show no heat change during mixing; Compounds involve energy absorption/release.

questions.question_text: Explain the principle of 8.2 Chemical Synthesis and Decomposition and state its scientific significance.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Heating iron and sulfur yields iron sulfide (non-magnetic compound with new traits). Electrolysis decomposes water into hydrogen and oxygen gases in 2:1 volume ratio. [A step further: Alloys] Stainless steel (Fe, Ni, Cr, C) and brass (Cu, Zn) are uniform solid metallic mixtures.
